answer: Each identity claims one yarrow plot and locks an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it files a signed log of plume drift over its plot, with its ivory card in frame. An auditor recomputes the drift from the wind table and source log for that plot, burning the bond on a miss over 3 percent or one card on two plots. The first costs 44; the kth costs 44+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5039 and 1000 fakes cost 2,541,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-plume ring fails, since a rented photo cannot match its wind row and ivory card serial. An honest operator pays 44 once and recovers the bond after audit.
